subject: Q2 OKR scoring & concise narratives for end-of-quarter QBR
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Redwood Partners Board <board@redwoodpartners.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 OKR scoring & concise narratives for end-of-quarter QBR

Team,

We need final OKR scores and short narratives for the QBR pack. Two asks: 1) complete the attached Q2_OKR_scoring_template.xlsx with numeric scores for each objective/key result (use percent progress or 0-1 scale, your choice) and 2) provide a 2-3 sentence narrative per objective that summarizes the outcome, the key driver, and one concise ask or open risk for the next quarter.

Please focus on candor: highlight wins and where we missed expectations — those are the most valuable signals for the exec deck. The QBR slide deadline is Friday EOD (June 27). I will consolidate narratives into the executive summary.

Quick formatting guidance for narratives (example):
- Objective: Reduce 95th pctl latency for hosted API to <= 40ms — 85% complete. Narrative: "Significant infra optimizations (heterogeneous kernel selection + prefix caching) reduced p95 from 62ms to 44ms. Remaining gap due to peak-path batching; request continued allocation for Dedicated capacity experiments."

Please attach your updated spreadsheet and any retrospective notes you want included. If you want to draft a short slide text, paste it inline.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | VP, Product | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Q2_OKR_scoring_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jun 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 OKR scoring & concise narratives for end-of-quarter QBR

Hannah — attaching the scoring sheet and a short retrospective for the Serving runtime objectives. High-level scores below (full detail in attachment):

- Objective A (Serving runtime performance): 85%
  Narrative: "Delivered kernel-selection pipeline and two quantization profiles; p95 improved by ~29% on common flows. Remaining 10–15% gap driven by tail latency from burst workloads; plan: dedicate one Reserved pool for sustained production experiments next quarter."

- Objective B (Throughput & cost efficiency): 78%
  Narrative: "Batching improvements and KV caching reduced token cost by ~18% for steady-state. Missed some targets during enterprise bursts; need smarter burst autoscale policies and additional monitoring hooks."

- Objective C (Reliability/SLOs): 92%
  Narrative: "SLA ramp and fallback policies worked as designed; only one customer-impacting incident (04-Jun) and automatic fallback prevented broader degradation."

Retrospective notes (short):
- Biggest win: kernel-selection reduced average unit cost without impacting latency for 95% of requests.
- Biggest regret: we did not prioritize dedicated burst capacity early enough; that slowed a few enterprise onboarding conversations.
- Ask for Q3: allocate a small reserved pool (2–4 GPUs) for controlled experiments on the new batching policy.

Attachment: Serving-runtime-retrospective.pdf; Q2_OKR_scoring_template.xlsx

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jun 2025 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 OKR scoring & concise narratives for end-of-quarter QBR

Thanks Evelyn — this looks solid. A couple of small edits for the exec narrative:
- For the performance objective, drop the internal-engineering jargon on "kernel-selection" in the single-line executive summary; lead with customer impact: "p95 latency improved 29%, enabling better user experience for low-latency features." Keep the engineering callout in the appendix.
- For throughput/cost, please quantify the customer impact where possible (e.g., % reduction in billed token cost to top 5 customers).

I added two quick bullets to the QBR narrative draft (attached in the consolidated deck link). Also agree we should call out the Dedicated pool ask as a clear action item with estimated cost/ROI.

On the incident note: can we include one-line remediation steps taken and the SLA credit (if any) we applied? That helps the board understand the operational posture.

Jonas
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Redwood Partners Board <board@redwoodpartners.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Consolidated Q2 narratives + next steps (slide deadline EOD)

Team — thank you for the fast turnaround. I consolidated the inputs into QBR-narrative-v1.md (attached) and updated the deck with the high-level lines Jonas suggested. Summary highlights for the executive slide:

- Product/Performance: p95 latency down ~29% QoQ; top-line customer feedback on latency features is positive. (Score: 85%)
- Cost/Throughput: ~18% reduction in steady-state token cost due to batching/KV cache; remaining hotspots during enterprise bursts. (Score: 78%)
- Reliability: SLAs met with one incident; fallback policies prevented escalation. (Score: 92%)

Open asks (to be listed on the "asks & risks" slide):
- Approve 2–4 GPU reserved pool for Dedicated experiments (Evelyn to provide estimated cost/ROI).
- Add one-line incident remediation and confirm whether a credit was issued (Ops to confirm).

Action items and deadlines:
- Lauren: finalize slide visuals and publish deck v1 to the shared drive by EOD Friday (June 27).
- Evelyn: paste the short serving-runtime appendix (2 bullets) into the deck by noon Friday.
- Jonas: provide the incident remediation line and cost/ROI note for the Dedicated pool by noon Friday.

If there are no objections, I will send the QBR deck to the board on Monday morning alongside a short one-page executive summary. Please reply with any corrections inline.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt | VP, Product | Redwood Inference

Attachments: QBR-narrative-v1.md; Q2_OKR_scoring_template.xlsx
